goal: Add harness-signals, a Rust background service that, per machine-local configuration, pulls errors and warnings from each tracked project's observability tools (Sentry polling, Nightwatch polling through its MCP server after a one-time OAuth sign-in, Nightwatch signed webhooks, or a custom command), maps them to architecture board cards, and feeds a live Heat layer on the dashboard board.
constraints: Each machine decides which projects it tracks through its own config file (HARNESS_CONFIG_HOME/signals.json); nothing is written into tracked projects.
Tokens and webhook secrets are read from files named in the config and never logged or stored in the harness DB.
Only minimal issue summaries are stored: titles truncated, no messages beyond the title, no request data or user identifiers.
The dashboard keeps holding no logic: the heat reaches it through the existing board.py overlay.
Nightwatch OAuth credentials live only in a 0600 file named in the config; access tokens are refreshed by the service and never logged or stored in the harness DB.

non_goals.description: No changes to the audit service's Rust code or routes.
No public exposure (tunnels) of the webhook port; that is the operator's choice.

acceptance.criterion: The signals crate builds cleanly and its tests (config, adapters, mapping, scoring, webhook signature, end-to-end poll against a fake Sentry) pass
board.py overlay passes the heat layer through
